headline: A 2016 law that sets Coast Guard funding and rules for fiscal years 2016 and 2017, plus many smaller changes to ships, staffing, property, and federal maritime programs.
what_it_does: The law authorizes money and personnel levels for the Coast Guard for fiscal years 2016 and 2017, and it sets new rules on air stations, icebreakers, promotions, pay notices, parental leave, and recreational boat certificates. It also changes shipping and navigation rules, reauthorizes the Federal Maritime Commission, and directs the transfer of several pieces of federal land to local governments and Alaska Native corporations. Many sections require the Coast Guard or other agencies to study an issue, issue regulations, or report to Congress.

who_it_affects.group: Coast Guard members and their families
who_it_affects.how: They get a new parental leave policy matched to Navy policy, a change to combat-related disability review rules, and a bar on involuntary retirement procedures for enlisted members with 20 or more years of service.

who_it_affects.group: Former Coast Guard members with debts to the government
who_it_affects.how: The Coast Guard may cancel part of a debt owed to the United States that was incurred while they were on active duty, if doing so is in the country's best interest.

who_it_affects.group: Residents near certain Coast Guard air facilities
who_it_affects.how: The Coast Guard cannot close listed air facilities before January 1, 2018, and later closures must meet search and rescue safety and response-time standards.

who_it_affects.group: Owners and operators of passenger vessels and fishing vessels
who_it_affects.how: Some survival craft and safety rules are delayed or changed, a loan set-aside of at least $59 million per year is created for fishing vessel repairs, and certain small fishing vessels are exempt from a classification requirement if they meet safety standards.
The Coast Guard must write rules making recreational vessel certificates valid for five years, and the boat model year is set to run from June 1 to July 31.
Their credentials, medical certificates, and radar endorsements are to be aligned on common expiration dates, and the Coast Guard must publish sample exam topics each year.
The Coast Guard must transfer 32 acres of federal land at Point Reyes Station to the county for affordable housing or another approved public benefit.

who_it_affects.group: Alaska Native corporations and residents of Tok, St. Paul Island, and Point Spencer
who_it_affects.how: The Coast Guard or Interior Department must convey specified land to Alaska Native corporations or the Tanana Chiefs' Conference, with environmental monitoring and access conditions attached.

who_it_affects.group: Coast Guard Academy and Coast Guard Auxiliary volunteers
who_it_affects.how: The Academy may partner with its alumni association to seek research grants, and the Auxiliary may patrol waterways that are navigable for Coast Guard purposes or that a state or local authority requests.

when_it_takes_effect: Most provisions take effect on the date of enactment, February 8, 2016, though many sections set specific later deadlines for studies, reports, regulations, and certain Coast Guard actions.
